purpose: Audit-ready records for the beginner Pesachim block. Learners see guided English; this file makes every source, teaching claim, and review gate inspectable before release.

primaryText.hebrew: אור לארבעה עשר בודקין את החמץ לאור הנר

translation.text: On the eve of the fourteenth, one searches for leaven by the light of a lamp.

encounters.learnerLevel: English-speaking beginner who can sound out Hebrew and is beginning to identify a Mishnah's case variables.
encounters.learningObjective: Separate the required action from its time and instrument before interpreting the discussion.

languageSupport.transliterationPolicy: On demand only; Hebrew remains visible.
languageSupport.grammarNote: Treat בודקין as the action, then attach the time and instrument phrases.
languageSupport.translationPath: A learner may reveal the guided English at any time.

encounters.context: The opening Mishnah states the bedikah practice. The opening Gemara examines the word אור; this lesson does not present a personal ruling about how to perform the practice.

assessment.bestAnswer: Name search as the action, the eve of the fourteenth as the time, and lamp light as the instrument.
assessment.rationale: This makes the case visible before analysis.
misconceptions: Treating the time as the action.
Treating the lamp as a separate legal case.
assessment.transferPrompt: Map the people, action, place, and time in an unfamiliar Mishnah before asking why.

encounters.safetyBoundary: Text study only; for personal Pesach practice, consult a qualified halakhic authority.

review.secondSourceContext: Mishnah Shabbat 1:1 changes the central variable from time/tool to people/place.
review.retrievalTrigger: Return after a missed case-map item or in the weekly review.

primaryText.editorialNormalization: The lesson isolates one word from its surrounding sugya for a vocabulary-and-context exercise.

encounters.learnerLevel: Beginner ready to notice that a compact Hebrew word may require textual context.
encounters.learningObjective: Ask which meaning of a short word fits this source and why.

glosses: אור — light; in context, also used for the eve
languageSupport.grammarNote: The learner is not asked to settle lexical history, only to notice ambiguity responsibly.
languageSupport.translationPath: Guided translation and surrounding case remain available.

encounters.context: The Gemara opens by asking about the sense of אור in the Mishnah's opening. The exercise teaches an interpretive question, not a final philological conclusion.

assessment.bestAnswer: Ask what אור means here and use the surrounding Mishnah and sugya to test the reading.
assessment.rationale: Context, rather than a guess from an isolated word, guides the reading.
misconceptions: Assuming every occurrence has one fixed English gloss.
Treating ambiguity as an error in the text.
assessment.transferPrompt: Flag one compact word in a new passage and state what context you would need.

encounters.safetyBoundary: This is guided textual interpretation, not a basis for issuing practice or deciding translation disputes.

review.secondSourceContext: A comparable compact-term exercise appears in a different tractate during cross-tractate transfer.
review.retrievalTrigger: Return when a learner misses the ambiguity check or saves a new vocabulary word.

primaryText.hebrew: אין חוששין שמא גררה חולדה מבית לבית

translation.text: We are not concerned that perhaps a weasel dragged [leaven] from house to house.

encounters.learnerLevel: Beginner who can distinguish an established obligation from a question about its practical limit.
encounters.learningObjective: Identify a limiting move that prevents an open-ended concern from making a practice impossible to complete.

glosses: אין חוששין — we are not concerned
languageSupport.grammarNote: Read the concern as a hypothetical that tests the edge of an established practice.
languageSupport.translationPath: Guided English may be shown alongside the Hebrew.

encounters.context: This is a boundary question within the Mishnah's treatment of searching. The teaching claim is about reading the limiting move, not an instruction for a learner's own Pesach preparation.

assessment.bestAnswer: The source sets a practical boundary rather than chasing an endless hypothetical.
assessment.rationale: The learner distinguishes the baseline practice from an open-ended extension.
misconceptions: Concluding that the search is optional.
Assuming every conceivable concern must be eliminated.
assessment.transferPrompt: In another source, identify the baseline case, the added concern, and the proposed boundary.

encounters.safetyBoundary: Text study only; no personal halakhic guidance is implied.

review.secondSourceContext: A later tractate's distinction can be compared as another way a legal discussion limits a case.
review.retrievalTrigger: Weekly review after a learner confuses the action with the boundary.
